reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and for a compliant finding no redline or counterparty comment is expected; none was proposed, and the rendered text is unchanged from the originals.

The cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right running against the Client; the only information flows (§3(e) real-time usage statistics and log files, §6 documentation supporting charges) run in the Customer's favour, so there is no frequency, notice, cost or system-access parameter to cap.

The two Vendor-side access items are correctly distinguished: §8(f) permits TrueLink to implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and §9 access is at Client's request solely for Y2K remediation at TrueLink's cost — neither is remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is absent.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is correctly treated as a false signal: the regex cannot match because no audit clause exists, and silence is more favourable to us than the preferred position; inserting parameters would concede an audit right we do not currently owe.

Classifying total absence of a Customer-adverse audit right as compliant is directionally correct for this customer-side rule, and the noted negotiation discipline (hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment, no system access) is appropriate internal evidence rather than a raised issue.
